subject: Post-call: Capacity incident and deployment path recommendation (Hosted -> Dedicated/Private)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emilia Torres <emilia.torres@finarc.com>
Cc: Luis Navarro <luis.navarro@finarc.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (capacity incident & deployment options)

Hi Emilia / Luis —

Thanks again for the call this morning. I wanted to capture the key points and recommended next steps so we have a single source of truth. Short summary below: 

- Incident: 07/18 03:45 PDT — sustained request surge on your production account caused repeated 503s and token throttles for 12 minutes; automated retry logic on your side increased concurrent spikes.
- Current hosted behavior: Your traffic pattern (short bursts of high concurrency) is pushing the hosted tenancy soft-limits in the region; capacity is still shared and we hit the transient queue backpressure.
- Primary ask from Finarc: 1) immediate mitigation for production reliability; 2) recommendations for preventing repeat incidents; 3) timeline / cost for moving to Dedicated capacity or Private VPC if needed.

Our recommended path (based on call and logs):
1) Short-term (hours): apply temporary routing policy to pin Finarc to a higher-priority Hosted pool and enable the 60s prefix-KV cache for your most common prompt templates — ops can do this with minimal config.
2) Near-term (3–7 days): spin a small Dedicated capacity pool (2 A100 equiv) in your preferred region, configure autoscale floor, and enable warm KV snapshots for fast cold-starts. This eliminates noisy-neighbor risk and gives predictable p95 latency.
3) Option for regulated workloads (2–4 weeks): Private VPC deployment (customer VPC peering) with on-prem gateway if you want complete network isolation and KMS control. This requires more lead time for infra changes and support onboarding.

Attached: draft SOW and a rough infra cutover plan.

Immediate asks for your team:
- Can you confirm urgency: would Dedicated be acceptable as a >90% likelihood next step, or do you require VPC/on-prem as the only acceptable long-term option?
- If Dedicated is acceptable, please reply with a preferred start window this week and the list of IP ranges we should allow for peering.

I'll coordinate internal sequencing once we have your preference. I cc'd Vanessa for pricing and Sean for the technical cutover.

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

- Estimated monthly cost for the 2x A100 equiv pool you mentioned (including a bump for warm cache storage)
- A concrete cutover calendar (minimal downtime) — we have a maintenance window nightly 02:00–04:00 UTC.

Subject: Internal: Finarc incident -> recommended Dedicated sizing & cutover plan

Folks —

Quick internal note following Emilia's reply. Logs reviewed (INF-7892) and CV of traffic indicates burst concurrency peaks ~1.8x their 95th percentile during the incident. Recommended immediate plan: 

- Sizing: provision Dedicated pool with 2x A100 equiv (model: redwood-gpu-2a100), reserved minimum 30 TPS sustained, autoscale up to 6 GPUs for sustained surges.
- Cache: enable prefix + KV snapshots; allocate 50GB persistent cache to reduce token generation on templated messages.
- Routing: set policy to route Finarc primary to Dedicated pool with fallback to hosted low-priority; set circuit-breaker at 75% saturation.
- Cutover timing: propose dry-run on 2026-07-20 02:30–03:00 UTC (within their nightly window) and full cutover 2026-07-21 02:00–03:00 UTC. Dry-run should be a traffic shadow followed by 10 minutes of validation.
- Risks: network peering not required for Dedicated; if they later request VPC, additional 2–3 week lead time for security review and KMS integration.

Pricing ask: draft SOW attached includes a monthly committed price + one-off onboarding fee. Aisha, please confirm the final numbers and the DocuSign flow (we can append the emergency SLA clause for 30 days if they need immediate SLA assurances).

Vanessa
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
